subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 3 – Lesson 8: Literacy – Reading a short story
outcomes: I can understand the story of Rasha and the orange bird.
I can use the words sketch, zoom, yell, whisper and smile.
I know the difference between amazed and amazing.

tf.s: At the start, Rasha had no ideas for a story.
tf.why: That was her problem at the beginning.

tf.s: The bird in the story could speak to Rasha.
tf.why: That is what made the bird unusual.

tf.s: The story begins and ends in Rasha’s bedroom.
tf.why: It starts and finishes in the same place.

tf.s: To whisper means to shout very loudly.
tf.why: To whisper means to say something very quietly.
When you yell, you speak very loudly.

tf.s: Rasha sketched a big orange bird with a long blue tail.
tf.why: Yes, she drew the bird in a quick sketch.

tf.s: “Amazed” describes a thing, and “amazing” describes how a person feels.
tf.why: It’s the other way: amazed is how you feel; amazing describes a thing.

tf.s: Rasha climbed onto the bird’s back because she was afraid.
tf.why: She climbed on because she really liked adventures.

tf.s: To zoom means to move very slowly.
tf.why: To zoom means to move very fast.

tf.s: A sketch is a quick drawing.
tf.why: Yes, a sketch is a quick, simple drawing.

o: She had no ideas for a story.
boxes.why: She needed an idea for a story.

boxes.q: What was unusual about the bird?
boxes.why: A talking bird is very unusual!

boxes.q: Where does the story begin and end?
boxes.why: It begins and ends in her bedroom.

boxes.q: Why did Rasha climb onto the bird’s back?
Complete: The bird ___ over the city.
Complete: I was ___ when I saw the talking bird.
boxes.why: Amazed tells us how a person feels.

boxes.q: What colour was the bird’s tail in Rasha’s sketch?
boxes.why: She sketched an orange bird with a long blue tail.

hunt.q: How a person feels: very surprised

o: a big orange bird with a long blue tail
mcq.why: She sketched a big orange bird.

mcq.q: Which tenses do we use to tell a story?
mcq.why: Stories use narrative tenses in the past.

mcq.q: How can you guess the meaning of a new word in a story?
o: Look at the pictures and the words around it.
mcq.why: Pictures and context help you guess meanings.

o: Rasha was amazed when the bird spoke.
Rasha was amazing when the bird spoke.
The bird zoomed over the city.
The bird zoomed quietly to her ear.
Rasha zoomed a picture with a pencil.
The bird was flying over the city when Rasha yelled.
The bird were flying over the city when Rasha yelled.
The bird was fly over the city when Rasha yelled.
The bird flying over the city when Rasha was yell.
mcq.why: was + -ing for the longer action; yelled for the shorter one.

mcq.q: Why do we say “an amazing adventure” and not “an amazed adventure”?
o: Amazing describes the thing; amazed describes how a person feels.
mcq.why: -ing describes the thing; -ed describes the feeling.

mcq.q: Was the orange thing by the window the bird or Rasha’s imagination? Which is a good opinion?
o: I think it was her imagination, because the story ends in her bedroom.
I think it was a skyscraper.
mcq.why: A good opinion gives an idea and a reason from the story.
Whisper is very quiet; yell is very loud.
